1/9  CMA  For Appellant : Mrs. A.Subadra for  Mr.V.Velu  For Respondents : R1 - Exparte  R2  M/s. C. Harini for  M/s. M. B.Gopalan Ass Ismail vs M/S. Jsr Infra Developers Pvt. Ltd on 19 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/14148620/
1  JUDGMENT
The claimant has preferred the above appeal seeking enhancement of the compensation.

2. The appellant/claimant had filed the claim petition stating that on 24.05.2016 at about 8:15 P.M,
while he was a travelling as a pillion rider in a motorcycle bearing Reg.No.TN-10-AJ-5321, a car bearing Reg.No.TN-09-BX-8276, belonging to the first respondent insured with the second respondent herein, came in the opposite direction and dashed against the motor cycle, as a result of which, the appellant sustained grievous injuries.
3. The first respondent remained ex-parte before the Tribunal.

4. The second respondent/Insurance company, filed a counter stating that the accident did not take place due to the negligence of the https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis driver of the car insured with them and therefore, they are not liable to pay compensation; and that in any case, the claim made by the appellant was excessive and prayed for dismissal of the claim petition.
5.
Before the Tribunal, the appellant examined himself as P.W.1 and marked seven documents as Exs.P1 to P7.
The Disability Certificate issued by the Medical Board was marked as Ex.C1.
The second respondent neither examined any witness nor marked any document.
6. The Tribunal after considering the oral and documentary evidence awarded total compensation of Rs.1,56,600/-, to the appellant.

7. The learned counsel for the appellant submitted that the Tribunal erred in awarding compensation by adopting Percentage method; that the appellant had established functional disability and hence, the Tribunal ought to have awarded compensation by adopting Multiplier method.
The learned counsel further submitted that the compensation under the other heads also requires enhancement and prayed for allowing of the appeal.
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis 8.
Since the first respondent remained ex-parte before the Tribunal, the learned counsel for the appellant made an endorsement to dispense with notice to the first respondent.
Hence, notice to the first respondent is dispensed with.

9. The learned counsel for the second respondent/Insurance Company, per contra, submitted that there is no evidence to show that the appellant had suffered any functional disability; that therefore,
the Tribunal was right in awarding compensation under the head disability by Percentage method.

The learned counsel further submitted that award of compensation even under the other heads is just and reasonable and prayed for dismissal of the appeal.

sentences.text: The only question involved in the instant appeal is whether the award of compensation is just and reasonable?
11. It is seen that the Medical Board had examined the appellant and had issued the Disability Certificate as Ex.C1.
They had assessed the disability as 15%.
The appellant had suffered fracture in t h e l e f t l e g F i b u l a , a s c o u l d b e s e e n f r o m E x s .
P 4 a n d P 5 a n d t h e D i s c h a r g e https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis Summary, Ex.P2.
However, there is no evidence on record to either suggest or infer that the appellant had suffered any functional disability.
Therefore, this Court is of the view that the award of the Tribunal under the head Disability by adopting Percentage method is just and reasonable and no interference is called for.
However, it is seen that the Tribunal had fixed the notional income for the deceased as Rs.10,000/- and had calculated the Loss of Earnings for a period of three months.

Considering the nature of the injuries, this Court is of the view that the compensation under the head Loss of Earnings can be enhanced since the appellant would have suffered Loss of Income for a period of six months.
The appellant would then be entitled to Rs.60,000/- (Rs.10,000/- X 6) under the said head.

In the circumstances, the award under the heads Transportation, Extra Nourishment and Attender Charges can be enhanced to Rs.10,000/-,
Rs.15,000/- and Rs.15,000/- respectively.
The compensation awarded under other heads is just and reasonable and hence, the same is confirmed.

Thus, the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is enhanced from Rs.1,56,600/- to Rs.2,06,600/- break-up as follows:-
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis S.
Description

Amount Amount Award No awarded by awarded by confirmed Tribunal this Court or (Rs) (Rs) enhanced or granted 1. Disability 75,000/- 75,000/- Confirmed 2. Pain and 30,000/- 30,000/- Confirmed Sufferings 3. Transportation 5,000/- 10,000/- Enhanced 4. Extra 10,000/- 15,000/- Enhanced Nourishment

5. Attender 6,600/- 15,000/- Enhanced Charges 6. Loss of 30,000/- 60,000/- Enhanced Earnings Total 1,56,600/- 2,05,000/-
Enhanced rounded off by to Rs.50,000/-
Rs.2,06,600 12.

With the above modification, this Civil Miscellaneous Appeal is partly allowed and the compensation awarded by the Tribunal at Rs.1,56,600/- is hereby enhanced to Rs.2,06,600/-
together with interest at 7.5% per annum (excluding the default period, if any) from the date of petition till the date of deposit.

It is made clear that the appellant is not entitled for any interest for the delay period of 392 days on the amount of https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis Rs.50,000/-,
enhanced by this Court as per the order of this Court dated 04.08.2023, made in C.M.P. No. 14150 Ismail vs M/S. Jsr Infra Developers Pvt. Ltd on 19 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/14148620/
3 of 2023 in C.M.A.SR.81992 of 2023.
